items.title: Albanese poised to kill off move to increase taxes on gas giants
items.description: The government will not increase taxes on gas giants in next month's budget, echoing the industry's argument that exporters are already paying tens of billions of dollars in taxes each year.

items.title: 'Sad for us': Hannah Clarke's parents step back from advocacy
items.description: After their daughter and three grandchildren were murdered, Sue and Lloyd Clarke began a charity to improve awareness of coercive control. Now they've decided they need to step back for their own health.

items.title: Award-winning Australian author David Malouf dies aged 92
items.description: Erudite and urbane, Malouf — perhaps most famous for his portrait of mid-century Brisbane in his 1975 novel Johnno — will be fondly remembered for his immeasurable contribution to Australian letters.

items.title: In dying, James Valentine taught us how to live. I'll miss being his sidekick
items.description: Children grew up with him, adults grew old with him, he kept us connected to our city, the world and each other. James helped us make sense of life and gave us permission to laugh at the absurdity of it all — and ourselves.

items.title: How the new eligibility test for NDIS participants could work
items.description: Labor's plan to create a new "assessment tool" to determine future NDIS eligibility based on functional need could backfire without the right settings, say experts.

items.title: Canavan's frosty foray into Farrer's campaign trail
items.description: This week the Albanese government pushed out a major reform ahead of the federal budget, the Nationals leader was out in the cold on the campaign trail and a former Treasury secretary had some choice words about the push for gas tax reform.

items.title: Sheraz risked his life translating in Afghanistan. His family paid the price
items.description: Sheraz worked with Australian and US troops in Afghanistan, as a result his family were targeted by the Taliban. This Anzac Day he's being heroed.

items.title: Court documents reveal fears Roberts-Smith was planning overseas move
items.description: Police were concerned war veteran Ben Roberts-Smith was attempting to move overseas and possibly to Singapore or Spain, court documents reveal.

items.title: Research for Congress raises doubts over AUKUS submarines
items.description: "Worrisome" construction delays plague the US Navy's submarine-building program, which Australia is relying on for its naval fleet.

items.title: Live: Iran attacks three cargo ships in strait, US Navy Secretary departs role
items.description: Iran has said it will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz as long as the US naval blockade remains in place. Follow live.

items.title: Kyle and Jackie O counter-sued for radio show contract breach
items.description: The company that broadcast the Kyle and Jackie O Show has launched a counter claim against the duo seeking damages for breach of contract, losses in profit and advertising revenue, and legal costs.

items.title: Billionaire's ex-staffer denied bail over $1.6m fraud allegations
items.description: Billionaire Judith Neilson's former secretary is accused of going on a $1.6m shopping spree using her employer's credit cards and bank information.

items.title: Russell Brand admits to sex with 16yo when he was 30
items.description: British actor and comedian Russell Brand, who is facing multiple sexual assault charges, has admitted to having sex with a 16-year-old when he was 30.

items.title: Live: Collard faces hearing to appeal nine-week ban over homophobic slur
items.description: St Kilda appeals the AFL's nine-week suspension handed to forward Lance Collard over a homophobic slur. Follow live.

items.title: The 'plunk' sound of rain makes seeds sprout faster, scientists find
items.description: Scientists say they have the first direct evidence that seeds can sense the sound of rain, and will sprout faster when they do.

items.title: Small WA town takes centre stage for Netflix series filming
items.description: There is a buzz about town in a small community north of Perth as filming begins for a new Netflix series.

items.title: Genesis Owusu goes out of his way to connect with fans — and detractors
items.description: Genesis Owusu today releases his new track Life Keeps Going from his upcoming third album Redstar Wu & the Worldwide Scourge, as he encourages engagement with people who don't agree with his political views.

items.title: War on hoons
items.description: You might have heard of hooning – in which people — usually young men — drift, race, and do burnouts on public roads. It happens across the country and has been around for decades. But, it’s getting bigger, louder and more visible. So are police crackdowns. Fines, car seizures and jail terms are all on the cards for people caught hooning. Despite the laws and serious dangers, people still do it. But, why?

items.title: Authors leave publisher after kids book scrapped for illustrator's comments
items.description: Writers including Evelyn Araluen and Randa Abdel-Fattah have left University of Queensland Press after the publisher axed publication of an Indigenous kids book over its illustrator's past "anti-Semitic" comments.

items.title: Fight over legal costs from Gina Rinehart judgement begins
items.description: A legal wrangle is underway over what costs mining heiress Gina Rinehart is liable for following last week's judgement in her epic court battle with the family of her father's former business partner.

items.title: Breaking: Three children attacked by dingoes in national park
items.description: Three children have been attacked by dingoes in Karijini National Park since Saturday, prompting a warning from authorities.

items.title: Danish head-on train collision injures at least 17
items.description: The incident happened north of Copenhagen, with images showing two yellow and grey trains, both with visible damage.

items.title: Homeless people told to surrender dogs in return for housing
items.description: Steve James said he was given the choice between surrendering his dog or continuing to be homeless.

items.title: Author of damning report into CFMEU says he did not keep 'trivial' records
items.description: The inquiry has been investigating alleged misconduct and violence within the Queensland branch of the Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union (CFMEU).

items.title: Actor suing Rebel Wilson agrees bath incident was 'strange and bizarre'
items.description: A young actor suing Rebel Wilson for defamation has given details in court about an incident at Bondi Beach, which she claims the Hollywood star has since mischaracterised.
